title: Answer-Free Self-Referential Critics: Training Solve-Then-Judge VLM Judges with Preference Labels but Without Ground-Truth Answers

contributions.purpose: Enable Solve-Then-Judge VLM critic training on preference-only datasets that lack ground-truth answer annotations.
contributions.mechanism: AF-SRC, an answer-free training paradigm that extracts pseudo-labels from preferred responses to supervise the critic's self-solve step, replacing ground-truth supervision.
contributions.evaluation: Validated on a physical reasoning benchmark against an oracle baseline with ground-truth access (13.27% vs 10.62% debiased preference accuracy).
contributions.source_quote: A novel answer-free training paradigm for Solve-Then-Judge VLM critics that derives pseudo-labels from preferred responses, enabling critic training on preference-only datasets.

contributions.purpose: Reduce shortcut behaviors (e.g., overfitting to option letters) caused by noisy preference-derived pseudo-labels.
contributions.mechanism: Group consistency gating that applies the self-prediction reward only when the model gives consistent predictions across option permutations.
contributions.evaluation: Improvements are consistent across all metrics, including MCQ accuracy of 72.38% vs 70.48% oracle vs 68.10% without self-prediction.
contributions.source_quote: A group consistency gating mechanism that filters self-prediction rewards based on model confidence across option permutations, reducing shortcut behaviors.

contributions.purpose: Show that preference-derived supervision can be at least as strong as ground-truth supervision for critic training.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison of AF-SRC (pseudo-labels plus consistency regularization) against an oracle baseline with ground-truth answers.
contributions.evaluation: AF-SRC achieves 13.27% debiased preference accuracy vs the oracle's 10.62%, a 150% recovery ratio on a physical reasoning benchmark.
contributions.source_quote: Empirical validation demonstrating that preference-derived pseudo-labels combined with consistency regularization provide stronger training signals than ground-truth answers alone, achieving 150% recovery ratio.

self_declared_provenance.quote: While these methods demonstrate the effectiveness of VLM critics, they typically require ground-truth answers or external reward models for training supervision.
These approaches focus primarily on text-only models or require answer verification mechanisms, leaving the challenge of answer-free critic training unexplored.

Recent work demonstrates that training critics to first solve a problem before judging candidate responses—the Solve-Then-Judge paradigm (Xiong et al., 2026)—improves judgment reliability by grounding evaluations in the critic's own understanding.

notes: Paper claims to EXCEED an oracle baseline that has ground-truth access (150% recovery ratio), an unusual better-than-oracle claim. Positions itself as removing the ground-truth requirement of the Solve-Then-Judge paradigm (Xiong et al. 2026 / PhyCritic).
